text: partnership firm was formed between Ramakanth a Land Lord and ' Surendarlal a businessman in Year 1982 in Hyderabad. Ramakanth was to provide his vacant land to the firm and Sunderlal was to provide Capital to the firm to construct a Cinema Theatre. Both the partners entered in to an agreement where in the partnership firm was to run the cinema theatre with Sunderlal being active partner and Ramakanth a sleeping partner. The sharing of Profits was to be in the ratio of 75% to Sunderlal and 25% to Ramakanth with a rider that ensured a minimum monthly payout of Rs 15,000 to Ramakanth even in the event of loss of business. The binding clause in the agreement was that Partnership firm was to operate for 25 years with an option of further extension of 10 years. Both Partners also agreed that partnership firm was to continue for the agreed period and shall not be dissolved before elapse of the time period. In 2000 Ramakanth filed a suit for dissolution of firm stating irregularities in book of accounts. During the pendency of the case Sunderlal Expired and his legal heirs continued the suit. How will the case be resolved, cite relevant sections and argue the case to its logical conclusion? Ashok an Allottee booked a 1500 Sq.ft. flat in Sunshine Builder’s 20 XYZ project located in Thane @ rate of Rs10000/Sq. ft on 2nd August 2017 by paying RS 5 Lac as Token. Sunshine Builder’s Allotment letter has condition that in event of cancellation of booking by allottees, builder reserved the right to forfeit 20% of flat cost. Ashok makes a second payment against flat of Rs 15 lacs. On 16th August 2017. Ashok from reliable market sources is given to understand that XYZ project does not have approval from Forest Wild Life Department on 30th August 2017 Ashok writes to Sunshine Builders on 2nd September seeking clarification on approvals. Suresh the Marketing Manager of Sunshine Developers shares via email dated 9th September 2017 the approvals received from Thane Municipal Corporation and also states that some other approvals are in advanced stages and awaited shortly. In meantime (around 12th September 2 Ashok happens to come across an advertisement by Sunshine Builders wherein a new building is being proposed in the space overlooking Ashok’s proposed flat in an area which was earlier shown as green space and a he also remembered paying a premium for the flat because of the Garden view. Ashok Cancels the booking on 15th September 2017 via Email wherein he states his reasons for cancellation as Lack of approval from Forest Department and changes in Master Layout particularly construction of new building in open space overlooking his proposed flat. Suresh schedules a meeting with Ashok on 15th October 2017wherein he shares the resolution passed by MOEF dated 13th October 2017 which shows the village in which XYZ project is being developed which was erroneously shown as part of ECO sensitive zone is not in ECO sensitive zone of Forest Department. Suresh also volunteers to reimburse the premium collected from Ashok for the promised views. He also cites that the sale brochure had a fine print stating that the builder reserved the rights to change the Master Plan. Suresh also explains that if Ashok chooses to cancel the booking, as per allotment letter the money already paid by Ashok stands forfeited. What are the options available for Ashok and under which sections of RERA? Write the judgement considering all available facts. Mr. Suresh entered into agreement for sale on 30th June 2012, to purchase a flat No. 501, K wing situated in Messrs Ashoka Builders Green Everest Project, Nakshahawadi, Paithan Road, Tal. & Dist. Aurangabad. Mr. Vimal also entered into an agreement with Ashoka Builders to purchase a flat no. 601 of K-Wing in respondents, same Green Everest Project. His agreement is of 28th March 2012. In the agreements executed in favour of both Suresh and Vimal, Clause- 11 reads that the developers agree to give the possession within 18 months from the date of execution of agreement. clause 11 of agreement also reads that non availability of Water shall be a one of the causes for extension of time. As on 15t May 2017 the developers have not given possession of the flats to Mr Suresh or to Mr Vimal. As per norm, as project has not received the OC as on 1% May 2017, the developers registered their project under RERA. b There was scarcity of water in Aurangabad during period 2013 to 2016. The Developers applied for MPCB permission on 23.7.2011 however MPCB asked them to stop the work by their letter dated 23.12.2013 and granted the permission by their letter dated 30.03.2014 MOEF issued stop work letter dated 09.06.2014 though Environmental clearance was applied for on 25.11.2011 Ultimately, Environmental Clearance was issued on 15.07.2016 Developers received only Rs. 13,59,160/- from Mr. Vimal and Rs14,35,000/- from Mr. Suresh as on 1%* May 2017. Developers on their own accord, agreed to pay compensation of Rs. 6,000/- per month to the complainants from October 2013 to August 2017 on account of the delay and it was to be adjusted against the total amount due from the complainants. On 15" May 2017, both Mr Suresh and Mr. Vimal filed separate complaints against developer for delay in possession. The developers applied for completion certificate on 1% November 2017 and are awaiting the same.
